senses: A meteorite consisting of rock containing chondrules.
ety: From Ancient Greek χόνδρος (khóndros, “grain”) + -ite. By surface analysis, chondr- + -ite.

senses: A person from the uplands.
Regular, periodic and repetitive, like a metronome.
Something exotic.
One who sculls; an athlete who participates in sculling races.
A boat rowed by one person with two sculls, or short oars.
examples: The first and second guns had been fired, and the scullers in their boats, each some ten yards apart from the other, are anxiously waiting the firing of the third, which is the signal for starting.

senses: A part of a line of poetry, especially in the distichal poetry of the Hebrew Bible and in early Germanic heroic verse such as Beowulf, where the line is composed of two (occasionally three) such parts.
ety: Borrowed from Ancient Greek στίχος (stíkhos, “line, row, verse”). Akin to στείχω (steíkhō, “I go”).

senses: An extended deck chair used for sunbathing or relaxing, typically by the sea or a pool.
A moustache.
The offspring of a cross between a horse sire and a zebra dam.
Any fibre having a nanoscale diameter.
One employed in soliciting the payment of debts.
The condition of being a transvestite.
a master, especially of music, in South Asia and the Middle East
ety: From Urdu استاد (ustād), from Classical Persian استاد (ustād, “master”).

senses: Having features common to pastoralism.
Using or relating to chemosynthesis.
A wax candle.
ety: Borrowed from French bougie (“wax candle”), after the Algerian city Bougie (Béjaïa), and the tapered, hand-dipped candles it made. The medical instruments were originally made from waxed linen. Doublet of bugia.

senses: A high-quality black tea made using young leaves, grown in Sri Lanka, India, Java and the Azores.
ety: Unclear; possibly from Hokkien 白毫 (pe̍h-ho, “white hair”) or Hokkien 白花 (pe̍h-hoe, “white flower”). See Tea leaf grading#Etymology. Compare to Russian ба́йховый (bájxovyj).

senses: An image of a person constructed out of bits of photographs of other people; an identikit.
ety: From photo + fit, from the British police force's Photofit system for constructing facial composites.
examples: The witness was called in to create a photofit resembling her memory of the attacker.

senses: A measure of the extent to which something is phytotoxic
A genre of instrumental folk music from Ukraine.
An individual composition in this genre.
ety: From Ukrainian ду́мка (dúmka), diminutive of ду́ма (dúma, “sung epic poem”).

senses: An artistic philosophy that emphasises instructional and informative qualities over mere entertainment.
A work, statement, etc. of this kind.
A deep purple colour, like that of the pansy.
ety: From Middle French pensée (“thought”), as the plant resembles someone that is in deep thought, with a lowered head. Doublet of pensée.

senses: Something puzzling or confusing.
The art of performing acrobatic gymnastic feats.
A spectacular display of agility.
The owner or operator of an art gallery
ety: From gallery + -ist, possibly by analogy with artist, or influenced by French galeriste; compare German Galerist. Attested since 1962, popular in US since 2000s.
examples: Artists become gallerists in order to ensure a viewing.
It’s an aesthetic that particularly appeals to the art dealers and gallerists who were scouring the Milan fringe shows for new talent last week.

senses: The pubococcygeal muscles.
A contraction of the pubococcygeal muscles, performed for the purpose of strengthening them.
ety: After Arnold Kegel. The surname is of German origin; see Kegel (“skittle, bowling pin”).
examples: Done for a few minutes a day, Kegels can ease childbirth, help with recovery, prevent incontinence — even improve your sex life.
Hop on top, I wanna ride / I do a kegel while it's inside

senses: A person who doodles.
Wheat grains that have been steamed, dried, and crushed; a staple of Middle Eastern cooking.
ety: From Ottoman Turkish بلغور (bulğur) (modern Turkish bulgur), by metathesis from older بورغول (burğul), from Arabic بُرْغُل (burḡul), from Persian برغول (barġul), پرغول (parġul).

senses: Having kneelike joints; able to bend at an abrupt angle.
ety: Learned borrowing from Latin geniculātus (“with bended knee”), from geniculum (“little knee”) + -ātus (participial adjective-forming suffix), see -ate (adjective-forming suffix).

senses: An agent (drug or other substance) that is bacteriostatic.
An alcoholic beverage, especially an inferior or illicit one and especially liquor such as whisky.
ety: Abbreviation of hoochinoo, name of a specific liquor, from Tlingit Xutsnoowú Ḵwáan, the group that produced it, from Hutsnuwu (“grizzly bear fort”), the name of the village on Admiralty Island in which they lived. From Tlingit xóots (“grizzly bear”).

senses: of, capable of, or causing illumination
An advocate of meninism.
To sniff or smell with the nose loudly and audibly.
To speak through the nose; to breathe through the nose when it is obstructed, so as to make a broken sound.
ety: Probably from Low German and Dutch snuffelen (“to snuffle”), equivalent to snuff + -le. Compare also Old English snofl (“snot, nasal mucus”), which might not have survived into Middle English.

senses: The art of projecting one's voice without moving the lips so that it appears to come from another source, such as a dummy.
Something that regresses, or causes regression.
A person or thing that regurgitates
A person or thing that muddles.
A tool used in muddling, used to mash and mix.
The fur of a chinchilla, used for clothing.
A variety of Persian cat with white fur and green eyes.
The line formed by the bottom edge of a skirt, dress, or coat; hem.
The height of this line, measured from the floor.
